why_now: Primary bind + T1–T5 showed conventional streams cannot close IIT/property gaps without regressive burden rename. Property map shows most non-URT school mills are debt-pledged. Tax reform alone is unlikely to reach the destination.
core_question: If conventional replacement taxes cannot do this without shifting the burden, what new productive revenue base must Constitutional Capitalism create?
transition_rule: Never retire a tax dollar until a recurring replacement dollar has been demonstrated, stress-tested, legally available, and reserved for the same essential obligations.
property_rule: Replace millage-class by millage-class — not one dramatic abolition date.

categories.name: Conventional public revenue
categories.role: Stability and bridge — cannot carry the whole transition at bound magnitudes
examples: Existing IIT / sales / corporate / severance / gaming / fees
Existing property millages (inventory only; not new capacity)
categories.counts_as_replacement_dollars: Only incremental new yield after protecting current obligations — not double-counting already-spent streams

categories.name: Prosperity-linked revenue
categories.role: Grows from economic activity without simply taxing individual labor or homeownership

categories.name: Productive public wealth
categories.role: State/community ownership or investment interests that produce recurring returns — the genuinely new balance-sheet requirement
